fit: fermented perilla leaf extract, rodent sleep recordings and induced sleep
assessment: Oral fermented perilla extract increased NREM sleep and slow-wave activity in animal recordings and shortened pentobarbital-induced sleep latency. The doctoral and subsequent journal reports are one family. The preparation and population differ from dried culinary shiso in Parkinson disease.

fit: historical paprika and salivary response study
assessment: The authorized preview confirms the general prior salivary-effect claim and research aim. Outcome pages remain gated. The preview cannot verify smoked preparation, specific results or drooling.

fit: fennel seed in shared Parkinson diet and composite motor examination
assessment: Appendix A lists fennel seed in a two-week diet offered to both intervention groups. The one-year composite UPDRS III result gives no separate freezing episodes or isolated toasted fennel exposure.

fit: plain dark chocolate versus cacao-free white chocolate and aggregate Parkinson motor score
assessment: The single-dose crossover tested 200 g of 80.1% cocoa dark chocolate without other supplements in 26 patients. The one-hour composite UPDRS III between-treatment effect was −0.54 points (95% CI −1.50 to 0.42). The original body gives no separate speech result or listener intelligibility test.

fit: registered one-week dark chocolate crossover with aggregate Parkinson symptom outcomes
assessment: A separate one-week protocol plans UPDRS and PDQ-39 along with several other measures. Status is Unknown and no outcomes are posted. Speech-item reporting and listener intelligibility remain unverified.

fit: pooled fish intake and objective olfactory impairment in older adults
assessment: Top versus bottom fish intake quartile associated with lower prevalent olfactory impairment, OR 0.65 (95% CI 0.44 to 0.96), but five-year incident OR was 1.23 (0.75 to 2.02). The food category does not isolate cod or baking and the cohort results are for community-dwelling older adults.

fit: topical cold-pressed pumpkin seed oil in a combination and a speech-containing oral mucositis composite
assessment: The combination improved the aggregate PROMS score versus benzydamine. PROMS includes speaking difficulty and speech restriction from mouth sores. The study reports no individual item changes, listener speech intelligibility or toasted oil exposure.

fit: homeopathic celery proving and acute hoarseness reports
assessment: One 6C or 30C prover had hoarseness with other respiratory symptoms. Fresh leaf identity, arm comparison and voice volume remain unverified.

fit: eight-herb perilla formula and global sleep quality in dyspepsia
assessment: PSQI medians were 14 to 12 versus 11 to 10, with respective within-arm p values .207 and .141. The original table supplies no randomized between-arm change and no perilla-specific or clinical Parkinson insomnia contrast.

fit: perilla-containing long-COVID crossover with registered day-28 sleep quality
assessment: The official record includes perilla leaf and PSQI but gives no results. Its liquid packet and tablet unit wording differ. Registration identity differs from the functional dyspepsia publication.

fit: ground anise and SF-36 vitality in functional dyspepsia
assessment: Week-12 mean vitality was 74.5 with anise powder versus 35.7 with cornstarch, after baselines of 51.3 and 52.8. Substantial control deterioration and distinct population and vitality endpoint limit transfer to Parkinson apathy.

fit: combined anise oil softgel and a premenstrual insomnia item
assessment: The insomnia item declined in both arms. Table 5 gives between-group p=.810. The comparison neither isolates anise nor uses ground seed or a Parkinson cohort.

fit: whole macadamia nuts and stool frequency and type in a crossover
assessment: Bowel frequency did not clearly differ. Bristol type p=.049 lacks direction and phase estimates. The companion and its supplements give no missing bowel data. Whole nuts and cold-pressed oil are different preparations.

fit: peanut butter and lower-limb function in older adults at risk of falls
assessment: Five-times sit-to-stand improved by an adjusted 1.23 s with peanut butter. The gait-speed result was inconclusive. The study gives no verified prospective fall-frequency result and did not use isolated oil.

fit: four-botanical blend including pomegranate peel and self-reported alertness
assessment: Day-21 predose alertness favored the blend in a follow-up versus placebo (p=.03), while the group-by-session interaction was p=.07. The blend, healthy cohort and proxy measure preclude a conclusion about raw arils and Parkinson daytime sleepiness.

fit: sequential pomegranate acai combination and self-reported alertness
assessment: The healthy cohort received the Peach Mango product first and Pomegranate Acai later. Alertness was planned. No result is posted and an isolated aril contrast is absent.

fit: okara-enriched tofu and acute salivary secretion during chewing
assessment: Enriched tofu elicited higher acute secretion in the author abstract. Baking and Parkinson drooling were not assessed. Saliva production and external loss are distinct outcomes.
